auditor_jane: Hi team — for the ISO evidence pack we need the end-to-end chain for the May 3rd P0 incident where a compromised CI token triggered an emergency key rotation. Can you provide: 1) RBAC change approvals and timeline, 2) KMS rotation logs (who/when/which key), 3) incident runbook execution trace and post-incident vuln triage notes?

maria: Hi @auditor_jane — we can assemble that. Quick answers up front: RBAC changes were a temporary service-account deprivilege (svc-batch-prod) between 03:12-03:45 UTC; KMS rotated key alias "alias/redwood-prod-emergency" at 03:20 UTC; runbook was executed from runbook-runner@ops (automation) with manual approval by ravi.

ravi: I approved at 03:15 UTC — I left a comment in the approval ticket: "Approve emergency rotation to contain token exposure" (ticket #SEC-2024-058).

aj: Adding the artifacts we should include: pre/post Terraform state snapshot, KMS CloudTrail export, Splunk query results for the suspicious token, RBAC approval thread export, and the runbook audit log (automation stdout).

maria: I'll drop commands and queries here for reproducibility. Splunk query we used to scope:
```
index=prod_auth sourcetype=app:auth token_id="tkn-xxxx" earliest=-2h@h latest=+1h@h | table _time user src_ip action resource
```

maria: KMS rotation evidence: CloudTrail extract command we used (aws cli):
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=RotateKey --start-time 2024-05-03T03:00:00Z --end-time 2024-05-03T03:30:00Z --query 'Events[].{time:EventTime,user:Username,arn:Resources[0].ARN}'
```

maria: Example CloudTrail line we exported: `2024-05-03T03:20:12Z | arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/sec-automation-role/session | RotateKey | arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345`

ravi: RBAC change record (from internal RBAC service): `change_id=rbac-7642, actor=ravi, target=svc-batch-prod, change=remove:role/producer, add:role/viewer, start=2024-05-03T03:12:30Z, end=2024-05-03T03:45:00Z, ticket=SEC-2024-058`

maria: Runbook execution trace (automation output snippet):
```
[03:14:53] runbook-runner: awaiting approval (ticket SEC-2024-058)
[03:15:10] ravi: approve
[03:15:20] runbook-runner: invoking kms:RotateKey alias/alias/redwood-prod-emergency -> key/abcd-ef01-2345
[03:20:12] runbook-runner: RotateKey succeeded, publishing key-change event to audit bucket s3://evidence-prod/incident-20240503/
[03:22:01] runbook-runner: restarting dependent services: deploy/kv-cache, deploy/stream-bridge
```

aj: For the audit bundle we'll include: `s3://evidence-prod/incident-20240503/` with manifest.json, cloudtrail-rotate.json, splunk-scope.csv, terraform-state-before.tfstate, terraform-state-after.tfstate, rbac-change.json, runbook-audit.log, ticket-SEC-2024-058.pdf

auditor_jane: Thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) How do you prove chain of custody for those S3 artifacts (presigned URLs or signed manifest)? 2) Any evidence that the rotated key was used to re-encrypt data or only to sign new tokens?

maria: Chain: we publish a signed manifest (SHA256) and a signed transfer log (runbook-runner writes transfer checksums to EvidenceLedger service). Example manifest line: `terraform-state-after.tfstate  sha256:3b7f... size:1.2MB  uploaded_by:runbook-runner  uploaded_at:2024-05-03T03:21:30Z` — manifest is signed by our CI signing key and stored in the same bucket with object lock enabled (governance mode) for 90 days. We'll include the signature file and the EvidenceLedger entry export.

ravi: To answer #2: we only rotated the KMS key material for the alias and re-wrapped active envelopes for newly issued tokens. We did not re-encrypt S3 data objects; the data keys for persistent storage remained the same CMK (different alias). We have a small script log showing envelope-rewraps for token store: `rewrap-token-store --key alias/redwood-prod-emergency --since 2024-05-03T03:20:00Z` output: `processed: 42 tokens, errors: 0` — include that log.

aj: Auditor wants an authoritative Splunk query output and a sha256 of that CSV. Maria, can you paste csv sha?

maria: splunk-scope.csv sha256: `a7f4d9c2b6b3c9f0e2f8c1b9d4e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e`

auditor_jane: Good. Also need proof that the RBAC change was expirable / temporary and that deprivilege was reverted.

ravi: RBAC policy shows automated revert job scheduled at 2024-05-03T03:44:00Z. Revert log: `rbac-reconciler: change rbac-7642 reverted, action=add:role/producer, removed=temp-lock, completed=2024-05-03T03:45:00Z` — attach rbac-reconciler.log line.

maria: Note on vuln triage: root cause was leaked CI token with overprivileged scope in pipeline A. Post-incident we: 1) applied least-privilege templates to all pipeline service accounts, 2) added token expiration safeguards to pipeline A, 3) added automation to detect long-lived tokens older than 12 hours. Short triage note: `vuln-2024-045: pipeline token leak -> mitigated; patch rolled to prod; follow-up ticket SEC-2024-062`

auditor_jane: Perfect. Final ask: can you export a single PDF evidence bundle with index that maps each control (e.g., A.9.2 access control) to the artifact file name? If yes, timeline?

maria: Yes — we'll generate an evidence-bundle.zip and a one-page control crosswalk PDF. ETA EOD today (2024-05-04 18:00 PDT). I'll upload to `s3://evidence-audit-delivery/auditor_jane/SEC-2024-058/` and post presigned URL with expiry 7 days.

aj: I'll prepare the manifest template for the crosswalk and ping @sec-bot to run a final integrity check before upload.

sec-bot: integrity-check queued for s3://evidence-audit-delivery/auditor_jane/SEC-2024-058/ — checking checksums and signatures.

oncall-bot: reminder: scheduled RBAC revert job completed at 2024-05-03T03:45:00Z — all services healthy.

auditor_jane: Great — please tag me when uploaded and include the presigned URL + signature file. Thanks all.

maria: will do. I'll attach all filenames in thread once upload is done. :thumbsup:
